_references.ASHRAE_HoF_2021: ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), Ch. 4 'Heat Transfer' (surface radiative properties) and Ch. 18 (sol-air / exterior surface absorptance)
_references.Bergman_2011: Bergman, Lavine, Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, 7th ed. (Wiley 2011), Tables A.11 (emissivity) and A.12 (solar radiative properties)
_references.CIBSE_A_2015: CIBSE Guide A: Environmental Design (2015), Ch. 3
_references.Warren_1982: Warren, S.G. (1982) 'Optical properties of snow', Reviews of Geophysics 20(1), 67-89
_references.Levinson_2007: Levinson, R., Berdahl, P., Akbari, H., Miller, W., Joedicke, I., Reilly, J., Suzuki, Y., Vondran, M. (2007) 'Methods of creating solar-reflective nonwhite surfaces and their application to residential roofing materials', Solar Energy Materials & Solar Cells 91(4), 304-314
_references.CRRC_directory: Cool Roof Rating Council, Rated Products Directory (coil-coated / painted metal roofing: measured initial solar reflectance and thermal emittance, ANSI/CRRC S100)
_references._note: Values are typical mid-range figures; absorptance varies with colour, soiling and age. Table numbers must be checked against the team's copy of each edition before the final report.

mud_plaster.source: Earth render, light-to-mid brown, range 0.6-0.75 (ASHRAE_HoF_2021; CIBSE_A_2015)

lime_whitewash.source: White lime wash, fresh ~0.2-0.3, aged/dusty 0.35-0.5 (ASHRAE_HoF_2021; CIBSE_A_2015)
lime_whitewash.notes: Common on Ladakhi buildings; strongly reduces opaque-wall solar gain.

white_paint.source: White acrylic paint alpha_S ~0.26, epsilon ~0.90 (Bergman_2011 Table A.12)

cement_render_grey.source: Light grey render / concrete-like surface, range 0.55-0.7 (ASHRAE_HoF_2021; Bergman_2011 Table A.12 concrete ~0.60)

dark_paint.source: Dark matte paints 0.85-0.97 (ASHRAE_HoF_2021; Bergman_2011 Table A.12)

galvanised_steel_new.source: New galvanised iron alpha ~0.65, epsilon ~0.13; weathered alpha 0.8-0.9, epsilon 0.2-0.3 (ASHRAE_HoF_2021)
galvanised_steel_new.notes: Low emissivity sharply cuts night-sky longwave loss (Phase 6) - matters for GI-sheet roofs.

prepainted_steel_sheet.display_name: Pre-painted galvanised steel sheet (PPGI), medium colour
prepainted_steel_sheet.source: Polyester/SMP coil-coated steel: thermal emittance 0.85-0.90 (Levinson_2007; CRRC_directory); solar absorptance by colour, see colour_variants
prepainted_steel_sheet.notes: Default outer finish for PUF-outermost constructions (adapters.default_outer_finish): an exposed PUF face is not buildable; PUF walls/roofs in practice are PPGI-clad sandwich panels. PPGI to IS 14246 (coating spec, not radiative properties).

light.source: White / off-white / light grey coil coatings, solar reflectance ~0.6-0.75 -> absorptance 0.25-0.40 (Levinson_2007; CRRC_directory)

medium.source: Mid grey / beige / terracotta / light green coil coatings, absorptance 0.5-0.7 (Levinson_2007; CRRC_directory)

dark.source: Dark green / dark blue / brown / charcoal coil coatings, absorptance 0.8-0.92 (Levinson_2007; CRRC_directory)

snow_fresh.source: Fresh snow albedo 0.8-0.9 (alpha 0.1-0.2), aged snow alpha 0.3-0.5; longwave emissivity 0.97-0.99 (Warren_1982)
snow_fresh.notes: Roof snow cover; the snow layer's thermal resistance is proposed separately (docs/materials_review_person2.md).
